h1: The 8 Printers Built to Jam Less of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Printers That Jam Less 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 printers built to jam less in 2026, from Brother laser models to Epson ink tank and budget inkjets for home offices.
summary: The Brother DCP-L2640DW is the printer least likely to give you trouble: a monochrome laser with a 250-sheet tray and duplex. The HL-L3220CDW adds color on the same paper path. The inkjets rank lower because wet ink makes them more sensitive to paper, though the Epson EcoTank ET-4800 and Brother INKvestment add scanning and help with clearing.
intro: No printer is jam proof, and the machine is rarely the main culprit. Humid reams, mixed sizes in one tray and a stack pushed past the fill line cause most misfeeds. What a good design can do is make jams rarer and less painful: a short, simple paper path, a tray that is not constantly refilled, and rollers you can reach without disassembling the machine.

We reviewed eight home office printers by spec sheet and scored them on the Primea framework, comparing engine type, tray capacity, duplex support, feeder hardware and display help. Each earns its place by how well its design should limit and ease jams. No pick comes with a guarantee, and the first rule is still to load paper correctly.

products.name: Brother DCP-L2640DW Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Printer
products.verdict: Laser reliability for a text heavy desk.
products.description:
The DCP-L2640DW is a compact monochrome laser with a 250-sheet tray, duplex printing and wireless and mobile support, and it works with Alexa. A laser fuses dry toner with heat, so there is no wet ink to cockle the page or leave it clinging to a roller, which is a common start to a misfeed on inkjets.

It ranks first because laser feeds tend to run steadier on plain office paper, and the tray holds enough that you refill less often. Refilling is when many jams start, since fresh paper is loaded crooked or overfull. The cost is that it prints only in black and sits in the $200 to $500 tier.

Buy it for contracts, letters and school work all day. If color becomes necessary, the HL-L3220CDW below shares the same tray size, so you lose none of the paper-handling benefit.
products.idealFor: Home offices with high text volume.
products.skipIf: You print photos or color charts.

products.name: Brother HL-L3220CDW Wireless Color Laser Printer
products.verdict: Laser paper handling with color when you need it.
products.description:
The HL-L3220CDW is a color laser rated at 19 ppm, with a 250-sheet tray, duplex and mobile compatibility, in the $200 to $500 tier. It uses the same laser approach as the DCP-L2640DW, which is the reason it ranks this high despite the extra cost.

It sits just under the monochrome Brother because color adds expense and four toner cartridges, and it is print-only, so there is no scanner or feeder. That is a quiet advantage for this guide: fewer moving parts in the paper path means fewer places for a sheet to catch. Against the inkjet all-in-ones, it is the calmer machine on plain paper.

Choose it for an office that prints mostly text but needs occasional color charts or logos. Skip it if you must scan or copy, since the HL-L3220CDW cannot, and you will need another device for paperwork.

products.name: Brother INKvestment MCF-J5010DW Wireless Color Inkjet All-in-One
products.verdict: An all-in-one with a touchscreen to walk you through misfeeds.
products.description:
The MCF-J5010DW brings a 2.7-inch touchscreen, INKvestment cartridges, automatic 2-sided printing and an automatic document feeder for copy and scan to a color inkjet body. The screen earns its place in a jam guide: when a sheet catches, the display can walk you through where it stopped and which door to open.

It ranks third, below both lasers, because inkjets tend to be more sensitive to paper and humidity. Against the cheaper inkjets that follow, it wins with a larger display and a proper feeder. The price, in the $200 to $500 tier, is laser money for inkjet behavior.

Buy it if you want scanning and color in one machine and prefer a clear on-screen walkthrough over guesswork. Skip it if you only print black text, where the Brother laser does the job with a simpler path.
products.idealFor: Small offices needing color and scanning.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-4800 Wireless All-in-One
products.verdict: An ink tank workhorse with a document feeder.
products.description:
The Epson EcoTank ET-4800 uses a cartridge-free ink tank system and includes an automatic document feeder, Ethernet and wireless connectivity, duplex printing, and scan, copy and fax, in the $100 to $200 tier. The feeder makes it the stronger choice here for stacks of paperwork.

It ranks fourth because tank machines are built for volume and ink cost, not for paper-path simplicity. The feeder, duplex unit and fax all add paper movement, and every extra turn is another place for a sheet to catch. The Brother units beat it on engine design for jam resistance. It does improve on the ET-2800 below in features.

Pick it for a home office that scans multi-page documents and wants wired network access. Skip it if you prefer laser, or never use fax, because the extra hardware adds clutter you pay for in space.
products.idealFor: Offices that scan and copy stacks.

products.name: Brother Work Smart MFC-J1360DW Wireless Color Inkjet All-in-One
products.verdict: Duplex and alerts without a laser price.
products.description:
The Work Smart MFC-J1360DW prints two-sided on its own and adds wireless printing and a 1.8-inch color display, with LC501 series cartridges, for $100 to $200. Duplex pulls a sheet back through the machine, and the small display at least shows an alert when something goes wrong.

It ranks fifth because the screen is smaller than the INKvestment's and the listing mentions no document feeder. It costs less than the MCF-J5010DW, though, and keeps the two-sided printing that many home offices use daily. A feeder-free design means one fewer mechanism to clear.

Buy it for a home office that wants duplex without paying laser prices. Skip it if you scan multi-page files, because without a feeder you place every page on the glass, and the 1.8-inch display is cramped for guided troubleshooting.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2800 Wireless Color All-in-One
products.verdict: A simple single tray path for standard paper.
products.description:
The ET-2800 is a cartridge-free ink tank all-in-one with a single tray feed path, wireless printing, and scan and copy, at budget tank pricing in the $100 to $200 tier. A single tray path gives each sheet fewer turns, so it is easy to follow and clear when something goes wrong.

It ranks sixth because it lacks the ET-4800's document feeder and duplex. The simplicity cuts both ways: with no feeder or duplex there is little to jam, but the machine is meant for standard paper and nothing else. Thick or specialty media push beyond what the listing supports.

Choose it for light to moderate everyday printing on plain paper. Skip it if you print on cardstock or other specialty media, or want to scan stacks, because every page of the stack goes on the glass by hand.
products.idealFor: Light everyday printing on plain paper.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: The cheapest machine here with a document feeder.
products.description:
The TR4720 pairs a standard-cartridge inkjet with an auto document feeder, built-in fax and mobile printing, in the $50 to $100 tier. It is the lowest-priced printer here that includes a feeder, which makes it the entry point for scanning stacks.

It ranks seventh because budget parts raise a durability question. Rollers in cheap feeders wear, and a feeder with worn rollers misfeeds more often than the day it was new. Cartridges also cost more per page than the tank models above, so a frequent printer pays for it twice.

Pick it for light home use where price and a basic feeder matter more than longevity. Skip it if you print daily, since a heavy schedule is where cheap rollers and standard cartridges show their limits, and the tank machines or lasers pay back faster.
products.idealFor: Light use on a tight budget.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: Compact, simple and best for one page at a time.
products.description:
The DeskJet 4355 prints, scans and copies wirelessly, with a single tray paper path, no feeder, standard cartridges and a 3-month Instant Ink trial. It has a compact footprint, in the $50 to $100 tier. Fewer mechanisms mean fewer places to jam, which is why a stripped-down machine can still make sense.

It ranks last because it lacks both a feeder and duplex, and standard cartridge ink is the costliest route in this ranking. The Instant Ink trial only softens that for three months, so read the subscription terms before enrolling.

Buy it for a single-user desk that prints one page at a time and values a small footprint. Skip it if you scan stacks or print more than a few pages most days, where the missing feeder and ink cost both become annoying.
products.idealFor: A single desk, one page at a time.

whatMatters.detail: A laser printer fuses dry toner with heat, while an inkjet sprays wet ink that must dry, and wet pages cling to rollers in humid rooms. Lasers handle plain office paper steadily. Choose laser if you print mostly text. The engine type is named in the product title, so read it before you read the feature list.

A 250-sheet tray reduces refills, and refilling is when many misfeeds start because paper gets loaded crooked or past the fill line. Overfilling is the classic cause of a jam. Check the tray capacity in the specs, load below the fill line and use one paper size per load. The two Brother lasers list 250 sheets.

Duplex units and document feeders each add paper movement. They are useful, but more paper path means more chances for a sheet to catch. Pick them only if you will use them. The Epson ET-4800 has both, the ET-2800 has neither, and the Brother DCP-L2640DW has duplex only. Match the extras to your actual work.

A single tray path gives paper fewer turns, so it is easier to clear and less likely to catch. The cost is flexibility: it suits plain paper, not thick or specialty stock. The Epson ET-2800 and HP DeskJet 4355 use one. Confirm the path in the listing, and note whether a feeder is present.

A touchscreen can walk you through clearing a jam, showing which door to open and where the sheet stopped. The Brother INKvestment has a 2.7-inch screen, and the MFC-J1360DW has a 1.8-inch display. Look for the display size in the specs. A bigger screen is easier to read when you are crouched beside the printer.

faq.q: Is there a printer that never jams?
faq.a: No. Humid paper and overfilled trays cause most jams, and curled sheets add to them. The picks here reduce risk through design, like a steady laser path in the Brother DCP-L2640DW, not through a guarantee.
Overfilling the tray and mixing paper sizes in one load. Load below the fill line, use fresh paper and keep to one size per load. Even the Brother lasers jam when the stack is crooked.

faq.q: Is laser worth it over inkjet?
faq.a: For text-heavy work, yes, because dry toner handles plain paper well. The Brother DCP-L2640DW costs more than the Epson ET-2800 but feeds plain paper steadily, with a 250-sheet tray that you refill less often.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Connect wirelessly via the display or app, then fan the paper before loading so the sheets separate cleanly. On a Brother with a touchscreen, follow the prompts, and on the HP DeskJet 4355, use the app setup.

Keep paper dry, clean rollers per the maker's guide and avoid curled sheets, which snag at the first roller. Store reams flat in a sealed bag, particularly if you feed an inkjet such as the TR4720 in a humid room.

faq.q: Can I print on thick paper?
faq.a: Check the listing first. The Epson ET-2800 is aimed at standard paper only, and a single tray path limits thick stock. A laser like the Brother HL-L3220CDW handles plain office weights best.

finalTake: For the fewest jams, the Brother DCP-L2640DW is the printer to buy: a laser engine, a 250-sheet tray and duplex. Add the HL-L3220CDW if you need color. Choose the Brother INKvestment or Epson ET-4800 when scanning matters more than a straight path, and always load paper below the fill line.
